scenes.title: Key ideas
items: TWAP (time-weighted average price) smooths manipulation, but lags fast moves.
scenes.vo: Smart contracts can't see market prices; oracles bring them in. Lending markets liquidate based on the oracle price, not the price you see on screen. First, Push oracles: a network updates prices on a schedule or when price moves past a deviation threshold. Next, Pull oracles: prices are fetched and verified when a transaction needs them. Then, T-wap (time-weighted average price) smooths manipulation, but lags fast moves. And finally, Failures: stale prices in outages, manipulation of thin markets, misconfigured feeds.

scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Your collateral is priced by a 30-minute T-wap. The market drops 10% in 5 minutes. Your screen shows minus 10%; the oracle shows maybe minus 2%. You feel liquidated and aren't yet, but you also can't rely on the lag: it catches up. Conversely, a thinly traded collateral token can be pushed up and borrowed against by an attacker.
